headline: A walking delivery robot called Iris is being tested on parcel rounds in northern England.
score_reason: New on 8 Oct; a real trial of a machine at work, but a short report with no developer, partner or scale named.
importance_line: Delivery workers on routes with stairs, narrow alleys and sharp corners could get help from a robot built for places other delivery robots struggle with; no developer, partner or timetable is named, and it is still a trial.
summary: Reuters reported in a video on 8 Oct 2026 that England has a new two-legged delivery robot called Iris, and Vietnam's state broadcaster VTV adds that it is being tested on parcel deliveries in northern England. VTV says Iris carries parcels of up to 15 kg at up to 6 km an hour, climbs stairs and crosses rough ground, and that its developers mean it to help delivery workers on hard routes rather than fully replace them; VTV also calls it Europe's first such delivery trial, a claim not checked independently.
notes: Reuters video page blocked (HTTP 401); details read on VTV via vietnam.vn (https://www.vietnam.vn/en/thu-nghiem-robot-giao-hang-hai-chan). Developer, town and partner not stated anywhere read. VTV does not credit Reuters, so the two are credited separately.
